newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo slams mortgage bank sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo slams mortgage bank sale plan.

text.p: Argentina's former economy minister Domingo Cavallo Thursday lambasted government plans to privatize the National Mortgage Bank (BHN) and the country's airports.
"The way it's happening, it's a terrible mistake," Cavallo told reporters one day after launching his candidacy as a congressional deputy in October's mid-term elections.

"They're going to use (BHN windfalls) for a public works program, with clear electoral aims, when what the country really needs is more domestic and foreign savings to lower the country risk so that there are better public works programs -- not just during one year but permanently," he added.
Argentina renews half of its 257-seat chamber of deputies in October mid-term elections.
Cavallo Wednesday launched his candidacy as deputy for the fledgling party Action for the Republic in the Federal Capital, saying his sights were set on the presidency in 1999 or 2003.

The outspoken minister was dismissed last July by President Carlos Menem after drawn-out clashes with leaders of the ruling Peronist party's old guard over his accusations of corruption and government-linked "mafias."

On the planned sale of the state mortgage bank, Cavallo said: "If the BHN is privatized, the revenue obtained should be used to reduce Argentine debt and improve Argentina's standing with those who decide whether or not to send their savings to our country."
The bill to sell off the bank was approved last week by the lower house finance and budget committee after long wrangling in Congress since it was announced in September.
The BHN has the largest assets of any Argentine bank at $4.3 billion.
Cavallo also criticized the planned airport privatization, saying it risks handing a monoply to "a group using front companies."
Cavallo's free market policies and peso-dollar convertibility program, launched in 1991, tamed runaway inflation and brought four years of strong economic growth.
